inputs.note: ratio_observed uses the point tag-knob (0.0094); the tag-knob CI includes 0 (no reliable knob effect), so the ratio's upper CI is unstable -- the robust inference is bin_ci95 excludes 0 while knob_ci95 includes 0. C-E17 discounts the SHOWING side for carry-over; knob uncertainty is handled separately below.

headline.carryover_source: single-MACE C-E2, CI-lower R^2=0.172 vs point 0.488
headline.sentence: Even crediting only the CI-lower carry-over (single-MACE R^2=0.172 vs the 0.488 point estimate), stability's chemistry-selection advantage is >= 24x the measured within-chemistry tag-knob (sensitivity: 14x under a variance-discount, 7x under the most punishing raw-R^2 discount); under the cleaner C-E9 ensemble label the floor is 30x. All these compare against the tag-knob's point effect (0.0094); the only way the ratio falls below 1x is to also credit the tag-knob its full upper-CI (0.071) -- but that knob CI includes 0, i.e. telling has no statistically reliable within-chemistry effect, so that is not a genuine telling win. Contrast with gap (800x) and density (91x), whose carry-over is near-perfect (R^2>=0.98) so they need essentially no discount: the headline should trust gap/density and caveat stability as >= 24x.
